title: Pointed regular strict local ind-etale limit of a divisor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $g\in R$ be a nonzerodivisor with regular quotient $R/(g)$, and let $y\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ contain $g$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There are a commutative ring $H$ in the same universe and a ring homomorphism $\iota:R\to H$ which is ind-etale (a filtered colimit of etale $R$-algebras). The ring $H$ is strictly henselian local (henselian with separably closed residue field), $H$ and $H/(\iota(g))$ are regular local, $\iota(g)$ is a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal of $H$, and some point $x\in\operatorname{Spec}H$ maps to $y$.

proof.text: Take Ω to be the algebraic closure of κ(y), and barY its canonical geometric point. Apply the retained upstream strictHenselizationResidue theorem to the full affine-neighbourhood colimit H = strictHenselization barY. This provides locality, strict henselianity, and the closed-point image. Recover b : R → H by full faithfulness of Spec from strictLocalizationToBase barY.

Apply the upstream strictHenselization_indEtale_of_affine_chart theorem to the identity affine chart and the identity presentation of Spec H. It proves b is ind-etale. The residue theorem identifies the structural image of the closed point with y. Apply PrimeSpectrum.asIdeal to identify the contraction of the maximal ideal with y; thus b(g) lies in the maximal ideal and is not a unit.

Apply the retained upstream strictHenselization_regular_divisor_quotient directly to R, g, barY and b. Its regular-ring and domain conclusions give a nonzero regular quotient H/(b(g)). IsLocalRing.of_surjective' makes that quotient local, and IsRegularLocalRing.of_isRegularRing_of_isLocalRing makes it regular local.

Apply the same upstream quotient theorem to 0; its hypotheses do not require a nonzerodivisor. Transport regularity of R to R/(0) using RingEquiv.quotientBot and Ideal.quotEquivOfEq. Zero is not a unit in the nonzero local ring H. The theorem gives regularity of H/(0), which transports back to H, and IsRegularLocalRing.of_isRegularRing_of_isLocalRing gives ambient regular locality.

Give H the algebra structure induced by b. The proved upstream instance Algebra.IndEtale.weaklyEtale supplies flatness. IsSMulRegular.of_flat transports injective multiplication by g. Assemble these properties with the closed point of H.

The proof uses the full affine-neighbourhood colimit directly; no small/full transport or small-model compatibility theorem is needed. All existential conclusions, the mathematical parent dependency, and the unit route are unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem regular_divisor_strict_local_limit
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (g : R) [IsRegularRing R]
    (hg : IsSMulRegular R g) [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {g})]
    (y : Spec R) (hy : g ∈ y.asIdeal) :
    ∃ (H : CommRingCat.{u}) (ι : R →+* H),
      ι.IndEtale ∧
      ∃ (_ : IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing H),
        IsRegularLocalRing H ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (H ⧸ Ideal.span {ι g}) ∧
        IsSMulRegular H (ι g) ∧
        ι g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal H ∧
        ∃ x : Spec H, (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι)) x = y
